transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, what finally pushed me to come in is that I keep getting up from my desk when I really shouldn't. Like, during sprint planning meetings for work, or even important personal things like mortgage calls. I know I should stay put, but I'll just suddenly feel like I need to go get a glass of water, or I'll decide I need to check something in the other room right then. It's just... becoming an issue.

Right before you get up, what are you feeling—is it a specific worry or anxious discomfort you're trying to relieve, or more just a general restlessness or urge to move with no particular worry attached?

It's not really a worry. I'm not anxious about the call or the meeting itself. It's definitely more of a general restlessness. 

Even when I’m sitting there looking completely calm on the outside, I just start to feel this... this pressure inside. It's like I absolutely need to move, or switch tasks, or at least do something with my hands. If I don't just get up and do it, it feels like I'm going to crawl out of my skin.
Thinking back, do you remember having this same kind of restlessness or difficulty staying seated and focused when you were a child, say before age 12?

Yeah, I do. I remember teachers in elementary school actually having to move my desk, or constantly reminding me to stay seated. I was just always popping up out of my chair. I also had a habit of talking before I was called on, or just... rushing through my assignments, even when I completely understood the work. I just had a really hard time staying still.
Does this restlessness and difficulty staying put cause problems for you in more than one area of your life right now—for example, both at work and in your personal relationships or home life?

Yeah, it does. It's actually started creating some friction both at work and at home. Because I keep getting up or stepping away, people are having to follow up with me a lot more than they used to. 

I just... I really worry that I’m becoming the unreliable one when it comes to planning tasks, whether that's with my dev team or with my family. It's frustrating because I really am trying hard to stay on top of things, but it's definitely getting in the way in both places.
Aside from the restlessness, do you often find it hard to stay focused on tasks or conversations, lose track of details, or misplace things like keys or paperwork on a regular basis?

Yeah, I do struggle with that. I mean, I'm okay with losing things—I have a pretty good system for my keys and stuff. But staying focused... that's definitely an issue. 

Like, I can start reviewing a pull request at work, or sit down to read through some mortgage documents at home, and I have every intention of just getting it done. But then, maybe five minutes later, I'll realize I've been staring at the exact same paragraph the whole time, and my brain is just... off somewhere else, thinking about five completely unrelated things. It's really hard to just stay locked in on what I'm supposed to be doing.

Has this restlessness and trouble focusing been pretty constant and ongoing throughout your life, or does it tend to come and go in distinct episodes—especially times when you also felt unusually elated, needed less sleep than normal, or had racing thoughts?

It's been pretty constant, honestly. I wouldn't say it comes and goes in episodes. It's just... kind of always there in the background. I definitely don't have times where I feel unusually elated or feel like I don't need to sleep. My sleep is pretty regular, actually. So yeah, it's really just an everyday thing I deal with, not something tied to any extreme moods or anything like that.
